value.text:
Lumière University Lyon 2 (Université Lumière-Lyon-II) is a public university in Lyon, France. Its head-office address is given as 18 quai Claude Bernard. The university's Berges du Rhône site occupies a historic area on the left bank of the river, while the Porte des Alpes campus extends into Bron and Saint-Priest. A French-language account also identifies the Rachais/MuMo and CFMI sites; these descriptions should not be conflated with a single precise campus coordinate.

Its institutional history is distinct from the earlier University of Lyon. Faculties that emerged in the nineteenth century were united under that older university in 1896. University Lyon 2 was established in December 1969 following the higher-education reforms of 1968. A further split in 1973 led to the creation of Lyon 3. In 1987, Lyon 2 adopted the Lumière name, honouring the Lumière brothers. The historical University of Lyon and the later regional University of Lyon groupings are separate entities.

The university teaches across arts, literature, languages, law, economics, management and the social sciences, as well as other stated fields. The French-language account enumerates six teaching and research faculties and several institutes, while describing a centre for French-language and cultural studies. Wikidata reports 29,996 students for 2018, whereas the French article's infobox gives 26,044 for 2023; these figures refer to different observation periods and should not be treated as a current headcount. A budget figure of €154.8 million is explicitly associated with 2022.
